headline: Islanders’ Ryan Pulock leaves game with upper-body injury
take:
Daily Faceoff reports that Islanders defenseman Ryan Pulock left Thursday's game with an upper-body injury after playing just two shifts, following an awkward board battle with Yakov Trenin. Daily Faceoff also reports that Senators forward Andre Burakovsky left his game with an upper-body injury, after missing four games with one earlier this season.

Pulock's absence would sting NYI. He's logging 18.9 minutes a night, yet the Islanders have controlled only 41.8 percent of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice at five-on-five so far this season. The team does a bit better with him off it, so the numbers don't paint him as a driver. Still, a second-pair defenseman who kills penalties isn't easy to replace for a 6-4-2 team whose goalies have saved 11.4 goals more than expected. Going by how the coach has used his players, Tony DeAngelo (16:09 a night) is next in line for those minutes. Burakovsky has played 11.9 minutes over seven games and has no points, so any impact on OTT is small.
